subject: Clarifying billing calculations for mixed streaming + session flows
messages:
From: James Liu <james.liu@acmehealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 23 May 2027 09:05:12 -0700
Subject: Clarify how you will bill mixed streaming + session usage

Hi Ben,

Quick follow-up from this morning's call — procurement needs one clear example of how Redwood will bill a hybrid flow we will run in production. Scenario below is simplified but representative:

- Customer sends a short instruction (30 input tokens) to open a session.
- The model returns a 2,200-token streamed completion (tokens emitted incrementally).
- The same session then does a quick retrieval + follow-up: 40 input tokens, 150 token completion (no streaming).

Questions procurement wants answered in writing:
1) How are the two completions billed (streamed vs non-streamed)?
2) Are there minimums or rounding applied per-request or per-session?
3) If Acme has a reserved commit, how do seat credits or committed units offset these calls?

If you can send a short worked example (numbers) and the exact contract language you'd expect, that will unblock our SOW and PO.

Thanks,
James

Subject: Re: Clarify how you will bill mixed streaming + session usage

James — thanks for the clear scenario. I've attached a small workbook (billing_examples_v1.xlsx) with line-item math; below is the short summary and the contract-friendly wording we usually propose. Camila / Soojin / Karthik: can you confirm the numbers and the recommended clause before I send to procurement?

High-level answer (short):
- We bill input + output tokens. Streaming output tokens are billed as they are produced (counts on the completion side).
- We apply per-call minimums and then aggregate at the invoice period for rounding/quantum.
- Reserved commits (Dedicated) offset usage after invoice aggregation according to the customer's SKU priorities (reserved units first, then overage at standard rates).

Worked example (hosted API pricing, illustrative unit prices):
- Input tokens: 30 + 40 = 70 tokens
- Output tokens: 2,200 (streamed) + 150 (non-streamed) = 2,350 tokens
- Subtotal tokens: 2,420 tokens

Billing rules applied in this example:
1) Per-call minimum: hosted API enforces a 25-token minimum per call (so the 30/40 inputs are above min; short calls <25 tokens would be rounded up to 25).
2) Rounding quantum: hosted calls are rounded up to the nearest 5-token increment at per-call level; invoice aggregates then apply the committed-unit offsets (see below).
3) Streaming: streamed tokens are counted exactly as emitted; if the stream is aborted mid-completion, billed tokens are those emitted up to abort.

Using the numbers above and a notional per-token rate of $0.0006:
- Billed tokens after per-call rounding: inputs unchanged, outputs rounded to nearest 5 => 2,350 -> 2,350 (already multiple of 5)
- Total billed tokens = 2,420 => $1.452

Reserved commit behavior (if Acme has a Dedicated or committed SKU):
- Daily aggregation: we aggregate usage per-day and apply committed units first. If Acme has a daily committed bucket (e.g., 10k tokens/day), that bucket reduces the billed overage.
- Seat credits: seat-based discounts are applied to invoice-level charges after usage aggregation (they do not change per-call rounding).

Suggested contract clause (short draft):
"Redwood bills per input and output token. Output tokens emitted via streaming are counted when emitted. Per-call minimums and rounding quanta are applied at the per-call level (hosted: 25-token minimum, 5-token rounding). Reserved units and seat credits are applied at the invoice aggregation step and reduce billed overage. See Exhibit A for worked examples."

Attachment: billing_examples_v1.xlsx (contains line-by-line math and two alternative rounding policies).

Adding a technical/ops confirmation to Ben's draft. I also updated the workbook with a second worksheet that shows the same scenario under Dedicated pricing (attached). Key clarifications we should surface to Acme procurement: 

1) Exact token accounting
- Input tokens: counted exactly at tokenization time.
- Output tokens (streamed): each emitted token is counted when produced; there is no additional latency-based rounding.
- Cache/prefix reuse: we apply a prefix-reuse credit when the same session reuses an identical prefix within a 24-hour window; duplicate token overlap is credited on the invoice as a negative line item. This avoids double-billing for short follow-ups that resend the same prompt material.

2) Rounding/minimums algorithm (how we compute billed units):
- Per-call step: compute input + output tokens for the call. If call tokens < per-call minimum, set billed_call_tokens = per-call minimum. Else billed_call_tokens = call_tokens rounded up to the per-call quantum.
- Per-call quantum: hosted = 5 tokens, dedicated = 50 tokens (dedicated reserved SKUs are coarser-granularity).
- Invoice aggregation: after summing billed_call_tokens across the invoice period, we apply committed-unit offsets (reserved units applied first), then apply seat credits or discounts to the monetary charge.

3) Minimums and exceptions
- Per-call minimums are only intended to prevent micro-chat abuse; for pilot customers or negotiated pilots we can set a lower per-call floor in the SOW.
- For long-running streams (>10k tokens) we recommend using a dedicated pricing path or a negotiated upper-bound price to avoid invoice surprises; this should be captured as an SLA paragraph.

4) Example edge-case: aborted reconnections
- If a client reconnects and the server retransmits the same token sequence (exact duplicates), the second set is eligible for the prefix-reuse credit if within 10 minutes; otherwise we bill both unless session replay is detected.

I'll flag the workbook changes and the alternate clause language for Ben to include. Camila, Karthik — if the AP team wants a different wording for Dedicated vs Hosted minimums, propose edits.

Thanks — a couple operational notes and a suggested contract insert for the redline: 

Operational notes:
- Cross-region fallback: when we route to a fallback model in a different cloud region, token counts are computed in the region that executed the inference; we do not double-bill but we tag the invoice line with region metadata for traceability. This matters if Acme has multi-region reserved buckets.
- Long completions: for completions longer than 50k tokens we recommend negotiation of a capped per-completion charge or a volumetric discount tier; otherwise the per-call quantum can create invoice spikes.

Suggested contract redline (language you can paste into the SOW):
"Redwood will bill per input and output token in accordance with the attached billing examples. For hosted API usage, per-call minimums of twenty-five (25) tokens and a rounding quantum of five (5) tokens apply. For Dedicated/Committed SKUs, a per-call minimum of fifty (50) tokens with a fifty (50)-token quantum applies unless otherwise negotiated. Reserved units will be applied to invoice-period aggregated billed tokens prior to calculation of overages. Redwood will provide prefix-reuse credits for identical prompt reuse within twenty-four (24) hours; such credits appear as negative usage line items on the invoice. Long-running single completions (>50,000 tokens) are subject to separate negotiation to prevent outsized invoice items."

If that's acceptable I can paste this into the DocuSign draft (acro_pricing_clause_draft.docx attached) and Ben can send to Acme procurement.
